transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, so… the main reason I’m here is because I was trying to get cleared for a logistics job, the kind where you’re moving freight and staying on your feet, and the clinic they sent me to said my weight was too low for them to clear me. They made it sound like it was a problem, like I needed to be checked out before they’d sign off.

But honestly, from my point of view, I don’t really see it that way. I mean, I look at myself and I just think I’m lean. Like, not soft, not weighed down—more like someone who can move quick, keep up, do the work. I’ve done physical work, and in my head being lighter just means I’m ready to go, you know? So I’m here because they told me I had to come, more than because I thought something was wrong.
Have you had any recent changes in your appetite, diet, or energy levels that might explain your weight?

I mean… I wouldn’t say there’s been some big change, like I got sick or suddenly couldn’t eat or anything like that. It’s more how I’ve been doing things for a while, I guess. Most days I keep it pretty simple—black coffee in the morning, maybe a boiled egg if I feel like I need something, or a little tuna, something clean like that.

And if I’m not actually on a shift moving freight or doing something where I’m burning it off, I kind of tell myself I don’t really need a full meal. Like, why eat a whole plate of food if I’m just going to be sitting around or not using it? That just feels unnecessary to me. So I don’t know if I’d call it appetite exactly. I can eat if I need to. I just try not to overdo it.
Have you noticed yourself losing weight without trying, or has your weight dropped below what is normal for you?

I wouldn’t say it’s been “without trying,” exactly… I mean, that makes it sound like it just happened to me and I had no part in it. I keep myself on the lighter side because, to me, that feels better for work. But the clinic for that logistics job, they weighed me and basically said I was too low for them to clear me, like it was outside what they considered okay.

I guess compared to what they think is normal, yeah, it’s low. But when I look in the mirror, I don’t see what they’re seeing. I just see someone lean, not weighed down, someone who can move fast and stay on his feet. For freight work, that seems like a good thing to me. So the number must have dropped below what they want, or I wouldn’t be sitting here, but I don’t feel like I look sick or anything.
Can you tell me approximately how much you currently weigh and how that compares to what you've weighed in the past, say, a year ago?

I don’t really have an exact number I’ve been tracking like that, not in the way they make it sound. I mean, the job clinic weighed me, and that’s when they said it was too low for them to clear me for the logistics work. They were treating it like, you know, some big red flag.

But to me, when I look at myself, I don’t see “too low.” I see lean. I see someone who can move quick, stay on his feet, not carry extra weight around while lifting and moving freight. That kind of work isn’t exactly easy on the body, so in my head being lighter is more like being ready for it.

As far as a year ago… I’m sure I was heavier at some point, but I don’t sit there comparing numbers month to month. I just know I’m here because their scale said I was under whatever line they use, and they wouldn’t sign off. That’s really the main reason this became an issue.
Has your weight loss been intentional, or have you noticed any weight loss that happened without changes to your diet or activity level?

Yeah… I mean, it’s intentional in the sense that I choose to keep it that way. It’s not like I’m eating normally and the weight is just falling off for no reason. I’ve got a routine, and I know it probably sounds strict when I say it out loud, but most days I’ll just do black coffee in the morning, maybe a boiled egg if I feel like I need something solid, or a little tuna—something small, something that doesn’t feel heavy.

And then I kind of judge the rest of the day by what I’m actually doing. If I’m on a shift and moving freight, lifting, walking around, then maybe I can justify more because I’m using it. But if I’m not working that kind of shift, if I’m just around or not burning it off, I tell myself I don’t really need a real meal. Like, I don’t see the point of eating a full plate if my body isn’t going to put it to use.

So no, I wouldn’t say it happened without changes. It’s more that I’ve been keeping my intake pretty tight on purpose. I don’t think of it as starving myself or anything dramatic like that, but yeah, I’m not just randomly losing weight while eating whatever.
Do you ever feel anxious about gaining weight or do you actively avoid certain foods or eating situations because you’re worried it might cause you to gain weight?

Yeah… I guess I do, if I’m being honest. I don’t like calling it “anxious,” because that makes it sound like I’m panicking or something, but certain foods get in my head.

Like rice, bread, anything greasy — fried stuff, heavy takeout, that kind of thing — I’ll eat it and then I can’t stop thinking about it afterward. It’s not just, “Oh, that was more than usual.” It’s like I can feel it sitting on me, or I start imagining it’s going to show up right away, like on my waist or in how my clothes fit. Even if I know, logically, one meal probably doesn’t work like that, it still bothers me.

And then the next morning I’ll check. Sometimes it’s the scale, sometimes it’s my belt, like which hole it’s on or whether it feels tighter. I’ll tell myself I’m just making sure I didn’t let myself go, but yeah, I suppose that means I’m worried about gaining. I mostly try to avoid those foods because it’s easier than dealing with that whole argument in my head afterward.
Do you have a strong fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even if others might see you as underweight?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t like the word “fat,” exactly, because I don’t walk around saying that to myself in those exact terms. But if I’m honest, yes, there’s a real fear there. Especially if I eat certain things.

Like rice, bread, greasy food—fried stuff, heavy food—those are the things that bother me. If I have them, it’s like I can’t just eat it and move on like other people seem to. I’ll keep thinking about it afterward, like it’s sitting on me, like it’s going to turn into weight right away. I know that probably sounds unreasonable, and maybe part of me knows one meal shouldn’t change everything overnight, but that doesn’t stop the feeling.

Then the next morning I’ll check. I’ll get on the scale, or I’ll check my belt, see if it feels tighter or if I’m still on the same hole. And if it feels different at all, even a little, I start thinking, “Okay, you let yourself go.” So yeah… even if other people say I’m too thin or under where I should be, I don’t really feel safe just eating whatever, because I’m worried it’ll catch up with me fast.
Do you believe you are overweight or need to lose more weight, even when others have told you that you’re already underweight?

Yeah… I suppose I do, though I don’t always phrase it to myself like, “I’m overweight.” It’s more like when I look in the mirror, especially around my stomach and my waist, I see places that don’t look right to me. Like if there’s any softness there, or if I don’t look smaller and tight, I feel like I’ve slipped.

And I know people have said I’m already too low, or that I don’t need to lose anything, but it doesn’t really land that way when I’m looking at myself. I used to be on the warehouse floor, moving all day, lifting, working hard, and in my head there’s this idea of what a disciplined man is supposed to look like. Lean, controlled, not letting himself go. So if my waist doesn’t look tight, I start thinking I’m not that man anymore.

It’s not even just about a number, exactly. It’s what I see in the mirror. My stomach especially. I’ll stand there and check from different angles, and if I don’t look small enough, I feel like I need to tighten things up more. So yes… even if other people say I’m underweight, I don’t feel finished or okay with it. I still feel like there’s more I need to lose, or at least that I can’t let myself get any bigger.
Have you ever made yourself vomit, taken laxatives, or done excessive amounts of exercise because you were worried about gaining weight or controlling your shape?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. I don’t think I’ve done those things in the way you’re asking, at least not like making myself throw up or using laxatives. That’s not really been my thing.

With exercise… I mean, I’ve always been someone who worked physically, so it’s hard for me to separate “too much” from just being active or trying to stay disciplined. I can get caught up in needing to move or feeling better if I’ve done something, but I don’t know if I’d call it excessive exactly. Maybe I’m not the best judge of that.

I guess what I can say is I do worry about my shape and weight, like we were talking about, but I’m not sitting here thinking, “I need to vomit,” or taking laxatives to fix it. It’s more that I try to be careful before it gets to that point.
